decisions.reason: As a homepage-featured product that is close to the firm’s established handcrafted seasonal range, it likely met or was near aspiration levels and fits existing skills with little problemistic pressure to withdraw.
This pyramid is strongly aligned with the firm’s core offer and was prominently presented, so management would likely see its early market response as satisfactory relative to aspiration levels.

Although more distant from the traditional range, its homepage placement suggests enough initial promise that, with some organisational slack in a growing industry, management would continue the trial rather than stop it immediately.

As a distant accessory product with only limited website prominence, it likely fell short of aspirations and would be a candidate for resource reallocation back to stronger core lines or better development projects.

This distant motif platform appears to have received weak market emphasis and, under bounded rationality, management would likely end a peripheral experiment that does not clearly justify its use of scarce craft and development resources.

A themed Christmas pyramid builds directly on the firm’s established competencies and brand, and its homepage visibility indicates results likely acceptable by the standards of the firm and comparable producers.
